ref: Epid. I, Case I
landmark: lived by the wall
opening: Philiscus lived by the wall.

ref: Epid. I, Case II
landmark: lived on Broadway near the place of Eualcidas
opening: Silenus lived on Broadway near the place of Eualcidas.

ref: Epid. I, Case III
opening: Herophon had acute fever; scanty stools with tenesmus at the beginning, afterwards becoming thin, bilious and fairly frequent.

ref: Epid. I, Case IV
opening: In Thasos the wife of Philinus gave birth to a daughter.

ref: Epid. I, Case V
landmark: lay sick near the founder
opening: The wife of Epicrates, who lay sick near the founder, when near her delivery was seized with severe rigor without, it was said, becoming warm, and the same symptoms occurred on the following day.

ref: Epid. I, Case VI
landmark: lay sick above the temple of Heracles
opening: Cleanactides, who lay sick above the temple of Heracles, was seized by an irregular fever.

ref: Epid. I, Case VII
opening: Meton was seized with fever, and painful heaviness in the loins.

ref: Epid. I, Case VIII
landmark: lived by the gully of Boétes
opening: Erasinus lived by the gully of Boétes.

ref: Epid. I, Case IX
opening: Crito, in Thasos, while walking about, was seized with a violent pain in the great toe.

ref: Epid. I, Case X
landmark: lay sick by the well of Phrynichides
opening: The man of Clazomenae, who lay sick by the well of Phrynichides, was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. I, Case XI
opening: The wife of Dromeades, after giving birth to a daughter, when everything had gone normally, on the second day was seized with rigor; acute fever.

ref: Epid. I, Case XII
opening: A man dined when hot and drank too much.

ref: Epid. I, Case XIII
landmark: lying sick by the shore
opening: A woman lying sick by the shore, who was three months gone with child, was seized with fever, and immediately began to feel pains in the loins.

ref: Epid. I, Case XIV
landmark: lay sick by the temple of Hera
opening: Melidia, who lay sick by the temple of Hera, began to suffer violent pain in the head, neck and chest.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case I
landmark: lived by the temple of Earth
opening: Pythion, who lived by the temple of Earth, was seized with trembling which began in the hands.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case II
landmark: lay sick by the new wall
opening: Hermocrates, who lay sick by the new wall, was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case III
landmark: lying sick in the garden of Delearces
opening: The man lying sick in the garden of Delearces had for a long time heaviness in the head and pain in the right temple.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case IV
opening: Philistes in Thasos had for a long time pain in the head, and at last fell into a state of stupor and took to his bed.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case V
landmark: lay sick in the house of Demaenetus
opening: Chaerion, who lay sick in the house of Demaenetus, was seized with fever after drinking.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case VI
opening: The maiden daughter of Euryanax was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case VII
landmark: lay sick in the house of Aristion
opening: The woman suffering from angina who lay sick in the house of Aristion began her complaint with indistinctness of speech.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case VIII
landmark: lay sick by the Liars’ Market
opening: The youth who lay sick by the Liars’ Market was seized with fever after unaccustomed fatigue, toil and running.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case IX
landmark: lodged with Tisamenus
opening: The woman who lodged with Tisamenus was in bed with a troublesome attack of inflammation of the upper bowel.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case X
landmark: one of the house of Pantimides
opening: A woman who was one of the house of Pantimides after a miscarriage was seized with fever on the first day.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case XI
opening: Another woman, after a miscarriage about the fifth month, the wife of Hicetas, was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. III, first series, Case XII
landmark: lay sick by the Liars’ Market
opening: A woman who lay sick by the Liars’ Market, after giving birth in a first and painful delivery to a male child, was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case I
landmark: lay sick beyond the temple of Artemis
opening: In Thasos the Parian who lay sick beyond the temple of Artemis was seized with acute fever, which at the beginning was continuous and ardent.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case II
landmark: lay sick by the Cold Water
opening: In Thasos the woman who lay sick by the Cold Water, on the third day after giving birth to a daughter without lochial discharge, was seized with acute fever accompanied by shivering.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case III
landmark: lay sick above the shrine of Heracles
opening: In Thasos Pythion, who lay sick above the shrine of Heracles, after labour, fatigue and careless living, was seized by violent rigor and acute fever.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case IV
opening: The patient suffering from phrenitis on the first day that he took to bed vomited copiously thin vomits of the colour of verdigris; much fever with shivering; continuous sweating all over; painful heaviness of head and neck; urine thin, with small, scattered substances floating in it, which did not settle.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case V
opening: In Larisa a bald man suddenly experienced pain in the right thigh.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case VI
opening: In Abdera Pericles was seized with acute fever, continuous and painful; much thirst; nausea; could not retain what he drank.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case VII
landmark: lay sick by the Sacred Way
opening: In Abdera the maiden who lay sick by the Sacred Way was seized with a fever of the ardent type.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case VIII
landmark: lay sick by the Thracian gate
opening: In Abdera Anaxion, who lay sick by the Thracian gate, was seized with acute fever.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case IX
opening: In Abdera Heropythus had pain in the head without taking to bed, but shortly afterwards was compelled to do so.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case X
opening: In Abdera Nicodemus after venery and drunkenness was seized with fever.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XI
opening: In Thasos a woman of gloomy temperament, after a grief with a reason for it, without taking to bed lost sleep and appetite, and suffered thirst and nausea.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XII
opening: In Larisa a maiden was seized with an acute fever of the ardent type.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XIII
opening: Apollonius in Abdera was ailing for a long time without being confined to bed.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XIV
opening: In Cyzicus a woman gave birth with difficult labour to twin daughters, and the lochial discharge was far from good.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XV
landmark: lay sick on the plain
opening: In Thasos the wife of Delearces, who lay sick on the plain, was seized after a grief with an acute fever with shivering.

ref: Epid. III, second series, Case XVI
opening: In Meliboea a youth took to his bed after being for a long time heated by drunkenness and sexual indulgence.
